- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) and price is trending down, model often under-forecasts; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing sharp drops.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially in 30d horizon), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often fails to capture the momentum — increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment acceleration.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30d horizon, model tends to overestimate late-period price (last 7–10 days) — apply a 3–5% downward correction if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.2), model often misreads trend — use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
